page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instructions. The server is equipped with 432.0 GB of system memory, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 27.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of an 885 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by bottom-quartile results in stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and stress-ng multi-core benchmarks placing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is stable, with cached read speeds reaching 733.31 GB/sec and uncached write speeds at 76.17 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET performance at 12.59 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 10.83 GB/sec also align with mid-range performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-16s_v3 represents a specialized resource allocation tradeoff. By constraining the vCPU count to 16 while retaining a massive 432.0 GB memory footprint, this configuration reduces software licensing costs tied to core counts while providing substantial memory capacity. This makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance, such as large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise relational databases, and memory-bound data processing pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine optimized for memory-intensive workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 2.6 GHz, it features an exceptionally high memory capacity of 432.0 GB (27.0 GB per vCPU) and an 885 GB local SSD. While single-core benchmark results are weak, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth consistently rank in the average tier. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory capacity without a high vCPU count, thereby minimizing core-based software licensing fees. It is best suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing.
